question: A 70-year-old male visits his primary care physician because of progressive weight loss. He has a 20-year history of smoking 2 packs of cigarettes a day and was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus 6 years ago. After physical examination, the physician tells the patient he suspects adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas. Which of the following physical examination findings would support the diagnosis:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking 2 packs of cigarettes a day -> increased risk of developing adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas -> 80% CHAIN: Diabetes mellitus diagnosis 6 years ago -> increased risk of pancreatic adenocarcinoma -> 70% CHAIN: Progressive weight loss -> common symptom of pancreatic adenocarcinoma -> 90% CHAIN: Suspected adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas -> possible palpable gallbladder due to obstruction of the bile duct -> 60% CHAIN: Suspected adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas -> possible lymphadenopathy of the umbilicus (Sister Mary Joseph's nodule) due to metastasis -> 70% CHAIN: Suspected adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas -> possible splenomegaly due to metastasis or compression of the splenic vein -> 60% CHAIN: Suspected adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas -> unlikely acanthosis nigricans or renal artery bruits as specific physical examination findings -> 80%
analysis: The physical examination finding that would support the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas in this patient is palpable gallbladder.
